title: Coordination & Cutoff Matrix for API / Console / Runtime Release
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Purpose: define a single coordination and cutoff matrix that aligns API, Console, and Runtime milestones, scope-lock criteria, release-note owners, communication triggers, and rollback policies. This ticket captures the cross-functional schedule, explicit cut criteria for feature inclusion, a decision matrix for exceptions, and the downstream marketing/ops tasks required for a coordinated launch across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The goal is to reduce last-minute scope churn and to ensure every release has a single owner for release notes, a signed-off risk assessment, and an operational rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: A published cutoff matrix spreadsheet (single source of truth) that defines T- deadlines for docs, code freeze, infra migrations, and rollout windows
Signed-off scope-lock list from PM, Eng, Design, Security, and Customer Success (documented in Drive) before T-10
Release notes template populated and assigned to notes_owner with review due at T-3
Communication plan for SRE, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success with runbooks and escalation contacts
Cut criteria enforced: any P0/P1 bug must be fixed before release; P2 requires an explicit exception logged in the matrix

cutoff_matrix_summary: Key milestones: Scope-lock at T-21, Code freeze at T-10, Release notes final at T-3, Deployment window T0. Cut criteria: P0/P1 blockers block release; perf regressions exceeding +20% p95 latency block; API contract changes require migration docs and customer notification; Console UX changes require canary + rollback plan; Private deployment packaging must pass security checklist.
go_to_market_tasks: Assign marketing TL;DR and technical deep-dive owners
Prepare customer-facing release notes and changelog entry
Update product pricing & feature pages if applicable
Coordinate Sales Engineering enablement doc and one-pager
Schedule webinar/demo for enterprise pilot customers
Publish SDK changelog and bump SDK minor versions where interface changes require it
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Last-minute perf regression from runtime kernel changes. Mitigation: run full perf harness on release candidate and hold canary with autoscaling guardrails.
Risk: Docs delay impacting enterprise rollout. Mitigation: prioritize enterprise-facing sections and create temporary in-console banner that links to draft notes.
Risk: Cross-team misalignment on private upgrade behavior. Mitigation: require a signed private-deploy compatibility checklist and schedule a dry-run upgrade with a test customer cluster.
Risk: Missing or incomplete release notes. Mitigation: enforce ownership and require notes submission before T-3; PM will gate merge of release branch if notes missing.
